title: 弹琴
author: 刘长卿
tr: 涼室無外響，空桑七弦分。所彈非新聲，俗耳安肯聞。月落未終曲，暗中泣湘君。如傳我心苦，千里蒼梧雲。

The seven strings of Kongsang ring distinct and clear.
What I play is no fashionable new tune,

In the dark the Xiang goddess seems to weep.

title: 新年作
author: 刘长卿
tr: 鄉心新歲切，天畔獨潸然。老至居人下，春歸在客先。嶺猨同旦暮，江柳共風煙。已是長沙傅，從今又幾年。

title: 江州重别薛六柳八二员外
author: 刘长卿
tr: 生涯豈料承優詔，世事空知學醉歌。江上月明胡鴈過，淮南木落楚山多。寄身且喜滄洲近，顧影無如白髮何。今日龍鍾人共棄，媿君猶遣慎風波。

title: 秋日登吴公台上寺远眺
author: 刘长卿
tr: 古臺搖落後，秋日望鄉心。野寺人來少，雲峰水隔深。夕陽依舊壘，寒磬滿空林。惆悵南朝事，長江獨至今。

author: 刘长卿

title: 晚次鄂州
author: 卢纶
tr: 雲開遠見漢陽城，猶是孤帆一日程。估客晝眠知浪靜，舟人夜語覺潮生。三湘衰鬢逢秋色，萬里歸心對月明。舊業已隨征戰盡，更堪江上鼓鼙聲。

Amid the dust of the world, when shall we meet again, I mean?

This time of parting fills the heart with sorrow deep and keen.
Your road leads out beyond the cold, drifting clouds,
I turn to return just as evening snow begins to fall between.
Orphaned young, I became a wanderer early in life,
After so much hardship, I met you all too late, I ween.
We cover our faces and weep, facing each other in vain,
Amid the dust of the world, when shall we meet again, I mean?

风尘扰攘不知后会在何期。

title: 夏日南亭怀辛大
author: 孟浩然
tr: 山光忽西落，池月漸東上。散髮乘夕涼，開軒臥閑敞。荷風送香氣，竹露滴清響。欲取鳴琴彈，恨無知音賞。感此懷故人，中宵勞夢想。

The moon above the pond rises slowly from the east.
I loose my hair to enjoy the evening cool,
Open the window and lie in a space of peace and ease.

Bamboo dew drips, making clear, resounding taps, at least.
I wish to take my resonant zither and play a tune,
But alas, there is no true friend to hear the feast.
This makes me long all the more for my old friend,
All through midnight my dreams of him do not cease.

title: 与高适薛据登慈恩寺浮图
author: 岑参
tr: 塔势如涌出，孤高耸天宫。登临出世界，蹬道盘虚空。突兀压神州，峥嵘如鬼工。四角碍白日，七层摩苍穹。下窥指高鸟，俯听闻惊风。连山若波涛，奔凑似朝东。青槐夹驰道，宫馆何玲珑。秋色从西来，苍然满关中。五陵北原上，万古青蒙蒙。净理了可悟，胜因夙所宗。誓将挂冠去，觉道资无穷。

en_body: The pagoda rises as if welling up from the earth,
Standing lone and tall, piercing the palaces of heaven.
Climbing it, one emerges beyond the world of men,
Stone steps spiral upward into the empty skies even.
Lofty and abrupt, it presses down upon the sacred land,
Soaring and rugged, as if carved by ghostly hands, riven.
Its four corners block the brilliant sun itself,
Its seventh story brushes against the dome of heaven.
Looking down, one can point to high-flying birds,
Bending an ear, one hears the rush of the wind striven.
The rolling ranges resemble waves upon the sea,
Rushing eastward as if paying homage to the ocean, leavened.
Green locust trees line the imperial carriageway,
Palaces and pavilions appear so exquisitely woven.
Autumn colors come rolling in from the west,
Pale and blue, filling all Guanzhong, unshriven.
Upon the northern plain where the Five Tombs lie,
For ten thousand ages green mists have been cloven.
The pure truth of Buddhism here can be fully grasped,
Good karma has long been what I have striven.
I swear I will hang up my official cap and retire,
For enlightenment brings blessings that never are riven.

baihua: 塔势如涌出，孤高耸天宫。登临出世界，蹬道盘虚空。突兀压神州，峥嵘如鬼工。四角碍白日，七层摩苍穹。下窥指高鸟，俯听闻惊风。连山若波涛，奔凑似朝东。青槐夹驰道，宫馆何玲珑。秋色从西来，苍然满关中。五陵北原上，万古青蒙蒙。净理了可悟，胜因夙所宗。誓将挂冠去，觉道资无穷。
en_lines: The pagoda rises as if welling up from the earth,
Standing lone and tall, piercing the palaces of heaven.
Climbing it, one emerges beyond the world of men,
Stone steps spiral upward into the empty skies even.
Lofty and abrupt, it presses down upon the sacred land,
Soaring and rugged, as if carved by ghostly hands, riven.
Its four corners block the brilliant sun itself,
Its seventh story brushes against the dome of heaven.
Looking down, one can point to high-flying birds,
Bending an ear, one hears the rush of the wind striven.
The rolling ranges resemble waves upon the sea,
Rushing eastward as if paying homage to the ocean, leavened.
Green locust trees line the imperial carriageway,
Palaces and pavilions appear so exquisitely woven.
Autumn colors come rolling in from the west,
Pale and blue, filling all Guanzhong, unshriven.
Upon the northern plain where the Five Tombs lie,
For ten thousand ages green mists have been cloven.
The pure truth of Buddhism here can be fully grasped,
Good karma has long been what I have striven.
I swear I will hang up my official cap and retire,
For enlightenment brings blessings that never are riven.

title: 寄左省杜拾遗
author: 岑参
tr: 聯步趨丹陛，分曹限紫微。曉隨天仗入，暮惹御香歸。白髮悲花落，青雲羨鳥飛。聖朝無闕事，自覺諫書稀。

title: 白雪歌送武判官归京
author: 岑参
tr: 北風捲地白草折，胡天八月即飛雪。忽然一夜春風來，千樹萬樹梨花開。散入珠簾濕羅幕，狐裘不煖錦衾薄。將軍角弓不得控，都護鐵衣冷難着。瀚海闌干百丈冰，愁雲黲淡萬里凝。中軍置酒飲歸客，胡琴琵琶與羌笛。紛紛暮雪下轅門，風掣紅旗凍不翻。輪臺東門送君去，去時雪滿天山路。山迴路轉不見君，雪上空留馬行處。

en_body: North winds sweep the earth, snapping white grass blades,
In the borderlands, already in the eighth month snow fills the skies.
Suddenly it is as if a spring breeze came overnight,
And thousands of pear trees bloomed before our eyes.
Snowflakes drift through pearl curtains, dampening silk screens,
Fox fur robes bring no warmth, brocade quilts feel thin likewise.
The general's horn bow is too frozen to draw,
The protector's iron armor is too cold to wear, to our surprise.
Across the vast desert ice stretches a hundred fathoms deep,
Sorrow-laden clouds hang frozen for ten thousand miles, no cries.
In the central camp wine is set to see the traveler home,
Hu lutes, pipas, and Qiang flutes play their melodies, sighs.
At dusk heavy snow falls thick outside the camp gate,
In the biting wind the red flag is frozen, it cannot rise.
At Luntai's eastern gate I see you off on your way,
As you leave, snow covers the roads to the Heavenly Mountains' size.
The road twists, the mountains turn, and you are lost from sight,
Only hoof prints remain in the snow, marking where you said goodbyes.

baihua: 北风卷地白草折，胡天八月即飞雪。忽然一夜春风来，千树万树梨花开。散入珠帘湿罗幕，狐裘不煖锦衾薄。将军角弓不得控，都护铁衣冷难着。瀚海阑干百丈冰，愁云黪淡万里凝。中军置酒饮归客，胡琴琵琶与羌笛。纷纷暮雪下辕门，风掣红旗冻不翻。轮台东门送君去，去时雪满天山路。山回路转不见君，雪上空留马行处。
en_lines: North winds sweep the earth, snapping white grass blades,
In the borderlands, already in the eighth month snow fills the skies.
Suddenly it is as if a spring breeze came overnight,
And thousands of pear trees bloomed before our eyes.
Snowflakes drift through pearl curtains, dampening silk screens,
Fox fur robes bring no warmth, brocade quilts feel thin likewise.
The general's horn bow is too frozen to draw,
The protector's iron armor is too cold to wear, to our surprise.
Across the vast desert ice stretches a hundred fathoms deep,
Sorrow-laden clouds hang frozen for ten thousand miles, no cries.
In the central camp wine is set to see the traveler home,
Hu lutes, pipas, and Qiang flutes play their melodies, sighs.
At dusk heavy snow falls thick outside the camp gate,
In the biting wind the red flag is frozen, it cannot rise.
At Luntai's eastern gate I see you off on your way,
As you leave, snow covers the roads to the Heavenly Mountains' size.
The road twists, the mountains turn, and you are lost from sight,
Only hoof prints remain in the snow, marking where you said goodbyes.

title: 走马川行奉送封大夫出师西征
author: 岑参
body: 君不见走马川行雪海边，

en_body: Have you not seen Zouma River, by the Sea of Snow?
Where vast yellow sands stretch upward to the sky.
In Luntai in the ninth month, fierce winds roar at night,
Stones in the river bed are as large as pecks, oh my!
They roll and tumble everywhere across the ground,
Driven by the howling gale that passes by.
The Xiongnu grass is yellow, their horses fat and strong,
West of the Golden Mountains dust and smoke rise high.
The great general of Han leads his army west on campaign,
At night the general never takes off his golden armor, nigh.
They march at midnight, spears and halberds clashing,
Wind cuts like a knife, slicing faces as they sigh.
Snow on horsehair mingles with steaming sweat, on dappled coats it freezes into ice in the blink of an eye.

title: 轮台歌奉送封大夫出师西征
author: 岑参

en_body: Above Luntai's walls the horn sounds through the night,
North of the city the Maotou star has fallen from the sky.
Urgent dispatches passed Quli last night, we hear,
The Chanyu's armies have come west of the Golden Mountains high.
From the watchtower westward dust darkens all the air,
Han troops have encamped north of Luntai, standing by.
The great general grasps the staff and marches west,
At dawn the flutes blow as the great army passes by.
War drums beat on four sides like a surging sea of snow,
The three armies' great shout shakes Yin Mountain, nigh.
War spirit at enemy camps rises up to the clouds,
White bones on the battlefield twist among grass roots, dry.
On Jian River wind blows fierce, snowflakes wide and thick,
At Shakou stones are frozen, horses' hooves slip and die.
Lord Imperial Secretary, you labor hard for the throne,
Vowing to repay your lord and pacify the border's cry.
Who has not seen names written in history since old times?
Today your deeds and fame shall all the ancients outvie.

Today I climb it as the dawn light begins to spread.
Clouds and mountains of Sanjin all turn toward the north,

That we may drink together in joy, o'er chrysanthemum cups bread.

author: 崔涂

The three peaks piercing heaven were not cut by human hand.
Before Emperor Wu's shrine the clouds are about to scatter,

en_lines: The lofty peaks of Mount Hua look down on Xianyang capital,
The three peaks piercing heaven were not cut by human hand.
Before Emperor Wu's shrine the clouds are about to scatter,
On the Immortal's Palm Peak the rain has just cleared, understand.
The River and Mountains pillow on Hangu Pass in the north, steep,
Post-road trees stretch west to Han altars flat across the land.
Let me ask you fame-and-profit seekers by the roadside,
Is it not better to learn eternal life here, on this strand?

Cassia blossoms shine bright and pure in autumn air.

Catching their fragrance on the wind, would love them there?
Plants and trees have their own inborn nature true,
Why should they seek a beauty's hand to pluck them, where?
